result.title: Improving Building Energy Efficiency with an Indoor Environmental World Model and Counterfactual Adaptive Learning
result.summary: Optimizing indoor climate systems plays a critical role in achieving the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals 11 and 13. However, indoor delayed thermodynamic responses and partial observability severely hinder existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods, which are primarily limited by implicit thermal inertia, occupancy dynamic prediction, and cumulative prediction errors during long-horizon rollouts. Thus, we propose a novel occupant-centric indoor climate control framework. It develops indoor environmental world models to predict future physical thermal baselines and dynamic occupancy, explicitly capturing latent thermal inertia. By formulating adaptive regulation as counterfactual advantage learning against future environments via a Branching Dueling Q-Network, and integrating a Held-Action TD-λ target, it effectively mitigates delayed credit assignment. Additionally, a proposed physics-aligned smoothness regularization suppresses high-frequency actuator fluctuations, potentially extending equipment service life. Experiments on SemiBuildingSim and Sinergym demonstrate that our method achieves a superior multi-objective trade-off. Compared to the best-performing methods, it further reduces energy consumption by 11.2%, occupant discomfort by 44.2%, and action fluctuation by 47.3%, achieving better sample efficiency and cross-region effectiveness. This interdisciplinary study offers an energy-efficient, occupant-centric AI solution for control science, building science, and energy sustainability.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向室内气候控制的 occupant-centric 框架：用室内环境世界模型预测未来热基线与占用动态以显式建模潜热惯性，并通过反事实优势学习与 Held-Action TD-λ 目标缓解延迟信用分配，辅以物理一致性平滑正则；在 SemiBuildingSim 与 Sinergym 上报告多目标权衡的改进。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「潜状态世界模型 + 延迟信用分配」的问题表述可能与 LVR 中跨 latent 步骤的贡献分配、部分可观测下证据筛选与长程 rollout 误差抑制存在概念类比，但该工作无视觉或语言推理成分，可供核查的迁移线索较为间接。
